Spool Gun Switch – Permits toggling between standard push gun welding with the Magnum® Pro 175L or aluminum welding with the Magnum® Pro 100SG Spool Gun. 2. Wire Drive Tension Pressure Adjustment – Permits increasing or decreasing the pressure applied to the top drive roll. 3. Wire Drive Spindle – Supports a 4-inch or 8-inch spool of wire. nodes.name: Cable liner

properties.name: Cable liner
properties.description: Cable liner

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

nodes.name: Wire drive motor

properties.name: Wire drive motor
properties.description: Wire drive motor

evidence.text: The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. features overload protection of the wire drive motor. If the motor becomes overloaded, the protection circuitry turns off the wire feed unit. Check for the proper size tip, liner, and drive rolls, for any obstructions or bends in the gun cable, and any other factors that would impede the wire feeding. To resume welding, simply pull the trigger. There is no circuit breaker to reset.

nodes.name: Work cable connections

properties.name: Work cable connections
properties.description: Work cable connections

evidence.text: column 1: Arc is unstable - Poor starting. | column 2: 1. Check for correct input voltage to machine. 2. Check for proper electrode polarity for process. 3. Check gun tip for wear or damage and proper size - Replace. 4. Check for proper gas and flow rate for process. (For MIG only.) 5. Check work cable for loose or faulty connections. 6. Check gun for damage or breaks. 7. Check for proper drive roll ori- entation and alignment. 8. Check liner for proper size. | column 3: If all recommended possible areas of misadjustment have been checked and the problem persists, Contact your local Lincoln Authorized Field Service Facility.

nodes.name: Allow the machine to cool down before welding

properties.name: Allow the machine to cool down before welding
properties.description: Allow the machine to cool down before welding
properties.instruction_text: Allow the machine to cool down before welding

evidence.text: If the duty cycle of the machine is exceeded, then the machine will thermally trip and the image shown will be displayed on the user interface. The machine must cool down before welding can be performed.

evidence.text: 14 INSTALLATION INSTALLATION ELECTRIC SHOCK can kill. • Do not touch electrically live parts or electrode with skin or wet clothing. Insulate yourself from work and ground. • Always wear dry insulating gloves. FUMES AND GASES can be danger- ous. • Keep your head out of fumes. • Use ventilation or exhaust to remove fumes from breathing zone. WELDING SPARKS can cause fire or explosion. • Keep flammable material away. • Do not weld on closed containers. ARC RAYS can burn eyes and skin. • Wear eye, ear and body protection. Observe all safety information throughout this manual. -------------------------------------------------------- INPUT AND GROUND CONNECTIONS  Before starting the installation, check with the local power company if there are any questions about whether your power supply is adequate for the voltage, amperes, phase, and frequency specified on the welder rating plate. Also be sure the planned installation will meet the U.S. National Electrical Code and local code requirements. This welder may be operated from a single phase line or from one phase of a two or three phase line.  The following warning decal is adhered to the input panel located on the back of the machine. The power cords supplied with the unit shall only be used with the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. unit.  The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. is shipped XJUIBIBSEXJSFE7 DPSEBOEB7UP7JOQVUBEBQUFS  Using the instructions in Figure B.2, have a qualified electrician connect a receptacle (Customer Supplied) or cable to the input power lines and the system ground per the U.S. National Electrical Code and any applicable local codes. For cords over 100 foot, larger copper wires should be used. Fuse the two hot lines with super lag type fuses as shown in the following diagram. The center contact in the receptacle is for the grounding connection. A green wire in the input cable connects this contact to the frame of the welder. This ensures proper grounding of the welder frame when the welder plug is inserted into a grounded receptacle. CONNECT TO A SYSTEM GROUNDING WIRE. SEE THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND/OR LOCAL CODES FOR OTHER DETAILS AND MEANS FOR PROPER GROUNDING. CONNECT TO HOT WIRES OF A THREE-WIRE, SINGLE PHASE SYSTEM. *.1035"/5/05&4 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JTIPVMECFDPOOFDUFEUPBEFEJDBUFECSFBLFS  FTQFDJBMMZXIFODPOOFDUFEUP7"$ 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JJTOPUSFDPNNFOEFEGPSVTFXJUIFYUFOTJPOT DPSET*GBOFYUFOTJPODPSENVTUCFVTFE FOTVSFJUJTDPOTUSVDUFEXJUI BNJOJNVNPGHBHFXJSFT LOCATION AND MOUNTING The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. will operate in harsh environments. Even so, it is important that preventative measures are followed in orderto assure long life, reliability, and safe operation. • The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. must be located in an area with circulation of clean air such that air movement in the back and out the front louvers. • Dirt and dust that can be drawn into the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. should be kept to a minimum. Failure to observe these precautions can result in excessive operating temperatures and nuisance thermal trips. HIGH FREQUENCY PROTECTION During operation, distance the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. from radio controlled machinery. The normal operation of the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. may adversely affect the operation of RF controlled equipment, which may result in bodily injury or damage to the equipment. evidence.text: 14 INSTALLATION INSTALLATION ELECTRIC SHOCK can kill. • Do not touch electrically live parts or electrode with skin or wet clothing. Insulate yourself from work and ground. • Always wear dry insulating gloves. FUMES AND GASES can be danger- ous. • Keep your head out of fumes. • Use ventilation or exhaust to remove fumes from breathing zone. WELDING SPARKS can cause fire or explosion. • Keep flammable material away. • Do not weld on closed containers. ARC RAYS can burn eyes and skin. • Wear eye, ear and body protection. Observe all safety information throughout this manual. -------------------------------------------------------- INPUT AND GROUND CONNECTIONS  Before starting the installation, check with the local power company if there are any questions about whether your power supply is adequate for the voltage, amperes, phase, and frequency specified on the welder rating plate. Also be sure the planned installation will meet the U.S. National Electrical Code and local code requirements. This welder may be operated from a single phase line or from one phase of a two or three phase line.  The following warning decal is adhered to the input panel located on the back of the machine. The power cords supplied with the unit shall only be used with the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. unit.  The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. is shipped XJUIBIBSEXJSFE7 DPSEBOEB7UP7JOQVUBEBQUFS  Using the instructions in Figure B.2, have a qualified electrician connect a receptacle (Customer Supplied) or cable to the input power lines and the system ground per the U.S. National Electrical Code and any applicable local codes. For cords over 100 foot, larger copper wires should be used. Fuse the two hot lines with super lag type fuses as shown in the following diagram. The center contact in the receptacle is for the grounding connection. A green wire in the input cable connects this contact to the frame of the welder. This ensures proper grounding of the welder frame when the welder plug is inserted into a grounded receptacle. CONNECT TO A SYSTEM GROUNDING WIRE. SEE THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND/OR LOCAL CODES FOR OTHER DETAILS AND MEANS FOR PROPER GROUNDING. Even so, it is important that preventative measures are followed in orderto assure long life, reliability, and safe operation. • The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. must be located in an area with circulation of clean air such that air movement in the back and out the front louvers. • Dirt and dust that can be drawn into the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. should be kept to a minimum. Failure to observe these precautions can result in excessive operating temperatures and nuisance thermal trips. HIGH FREQUENCY PROTECTION During operation, distance the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. from radio controlled machinery. The normal operation of the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. may adversely affect the operation of RF controlled equipment, which may result in bodily injury or damage to the equipment. evidence.text: The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. features overload protection of the wire drive motor. If the motor becomes overloaded, the protection circuitry turns off the wire feed unit. Check for the proper size tip, liner, and drive rolls, for any obstructions or bends in the gun cable, and any other factors that would impede the wire feeding. To resume welding, simply pull the trigger. There is no circuit breaker to reset.

evidence.text: 14 INSTALLATION INSTALLATION ELECTRIC SHOCK can kill. • Do not touch electrically live parts or electrode with skin or wet clothing. Insulate yourself from work and ground. • Always wear dry insulating gloves. FUMES AND GASES can be danger- ous. • Keep your head out of fumes. • Use ventilation or exhaust to remove fumes from breathing zone. WELDING SPARKS can cause fire or explosion. • Keep flammable material away. • Do not weld on closed containers. ARC RAYS can burn eyes and skin. • Wear eye, ear and body protection. Observe all safety information throughout this manual. -------------------------------------------------------- INPUT AND GROUND CONNECTIONS  Before starting the installation, check with the local power company if there are any questions about whether your power supply is adequate for the voltage, amperes, phase, and frequency specified on the welder rating plate. Also be sure the planned installation will meet the U.S. National Electrical Code and local code requirements. This welder may be operated from a single phase line or from one phase of a two or three phase line.  The following warning decal is adhered to the input panel located on the back of the machine. The power cords supplied with the unit shall only be used with the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. unit.  The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. is shipped XJUIBIBSEXJSFE7 DPSEBOEB7UP7JOQVUBEBQUFS  Using the instructions in Figure B.2, have a qualified electrician connect a receptacle (Customer Supplied) or cable to the input power lines and the system ground per the U.S. National Electrical Code and any applicable local codes. For cords over 100 foot, larger copper wires should be used. Fuse the two hot lines with super lag type fuses as shown in the following diagram. The center contact in the receptacle is for the grounding connection. A green wire in the input cable connects this contact to the frame of the welder. This ensures proper grounding of the welder frame when the welder plug is inserted into a grounded receptacle. CONNECT TO A SYSTEM GROUNDING WIRE. SEE THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND/OR LOCAL CODES FOR OTHER DETAILS AND MEANS FOR PROPER GROUNDING. Even so, it is important that preventative measures are followed in orderto assure long life, reliability, and safe operation. • The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. must be located in an area with circulation of clean air such that air movement in the back and out the front louvers. • Dirt and dust that can be drawn into the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. should be kept to a minimum. Failure to observe these precautions can result in excessive operating temperatures and nuisance thermal trips. HIGH FREQUENCY PROTECTION During operation, distance the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. from radio controlled machinery. The normal operation of the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. may adversely affect the operation of RF controlled equipment, which may result in bodily injury or damage to the equipment. properties.description: Dirt-clogged air passages

evidence.text: GENERAL MAINTENANCE In extremely dusty locations, dirt may clog the air passages causing the welder to run hot. Blow dirt out of the welder with low-pressure air at regular intervals to eliminate excessive dirt and dust build-up on internal parts.

After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

nodes.name: Duty cycle exceeded

properties.name: Duty cycle exceeded
properties.description: Duty cycle exceeded

evidence.text: The duty cycle is the “on” time (based on a 10 minute interval) the user can weld with the machine at a specific output without causing a thermal trip.

If the duty cycle of the machine is exceeded, then the machine will thermally trip and the image shown will be displayed on the user interface. The machine must cool down before welding can be performed.

evidence.text: The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. features overload protection of the wire drive motor. If the motor becomes overloaded, the protection circuitry turns off the wire feed unit. evidence.text: 14 INSTALLATION INSTALLATION ELECTRIC SHOCK can kill. • Do not touch electrically live parts or electrode with skin or wet clothing. Insulate yourself from work and ground. • Always wear dry insulating gloves. FUMES AND GASES can be danger- ous. • Keep your head out of fumes. • Use ventilation or exhaust to remove fumes from breathing zone. WELDING SPARKS can cause fire or explosion. • Keep flammable material away. • Do not weld on closed containers. ARC RAYS can burn eyes and skin. • Wear eye, ear and body protection. Observe all safety information throughout this manual. -------------------------------------------------------- INPUT AND GROUND CONNECTIONS  Before starting the installation, check with the local power company if there are any questions about whether your power supply is adequate for the voltage, amperes, phase, and frequency specified on the welder rating plate. Also be sure the planned installation will meet the U.S. National Electrical Code and local code requirements. This welder may be operated from a single phase line or from one phase of a two or three phase line.  The following warning decal is adhered to the input panel located on the back of the machine. The power cords supplied with the unit shall only be used with the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. unit.  The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. is shipped XJUIBIBSEXJSFE7 DPSEBOEB7UP7JOQVUBEBQUFS  Using the instructions in Figure B.2, have a qualified electrician connect a receptacle (Customer Supplied) or cable to the input power lines and the system ground per the U.S. National Electrical Code and any applicable local codes. For cords over 100 foot, larger copper wires should be used. Fuse the two hot lines with super lag type fuses as shown in the following diagram. The center contact in the receptacle is for the grounding connection. A green wire in the input cable connects this contact to the frame of the welder. This ensures proper grounding of the welder frame when the welder plug is inserted into a grounded receptacle. CONNECT TO A SYSTEM GROUNDING WIRE. SEE THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND/OR LOCAL CODES FOR OTHER DETAILS AND MEANS FOR PROPER GROUNDING. CONNECT TO HOT WIRES OF A THREE-WIRE, SINGLE PHASE SYSTEM. *.1035"/5/05&4 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JTIPVMECFDPOOFDUFEUPBEFEJDBUFECSFBLFS  FTQFDJBMMZXIFODPOOFDUFEUP7"$ 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JJTOPUSFDPNNFOEFEGPSVTFXJUIFYUFOTJPOT DPSET*GBOFYUFOTJPODPSENVTUCFVTFE FOTVSFJUJTDPOTUSVDUFEXJUI BNJOJNVNPGHBHFXJSFT LOCATION AND MOUNTING The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. will operate in harsh environments. Even so, it is important that preventative measures are followed in orderto assure long life, reliability, and safe operation. • The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. must be located in an area with circulation of clean air such that air movement in the back and out the front louvers. • Dirt and dust that can be drawn into the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. should be kept to a minimum. Failure to observe these precautions can result in excessive operating temperatures and nuisance thermal trips. HIGH FREQUENCY PROTECTION During operation, distance the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. from radio controlled machinery. The normal operation of the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. may adversely affect the operation of RF controlled equipment, which may result in bodily injury or damage to the equipment. nodes.name: Excessive operating temperatures

properties.name: Excessive operating temperatures
properties.description: Excessive operating temperatures

evidence.text: 14 INSTALLATION INSTALLATION ELECTRIC SHOCK can kill. • Do not touch electrically live parts or electrode with skin or wet clothing. Insulate yourself from work and ground. • Always wear dry insulating gloves. FUMES AND GASES can be danger- ous. • Keep your head out of fumes. • Use ventilation or exhaust to remove fumes from breathing zone. WELDING SPARKS can cause fire or explosion. • Keep flammable material away. • Do not weld on closed containers. ARC RAYS can burn eyes and skin. • Wear eye, ear and body protection. Observe all safety information throughout this manual. -------------------------------------------------------- INPUT AND GROUND CONNECTIONS  Before starting the installation, check with the local power company if there are any questions about whether your power supply is adequate for the voltage, amperes, phase, and frequency specified on the welder rating plate. Also be sure the planned installation will meet the U.S. National Electrical Code and local code requirements. This welder may be operated from a single phase line or from one phase of a two or three phase line.  The following warning decal is adhered to the input panel located on the back of the machine. The power cords supplied with the unit shall only be used with the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. unit.  The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. is shipped XJUIBIBSEXJSFE7 DPSEBOEB7UP7JOQVUBEBQUFS  Using the instructions in Figure B.2, have a qualified electrician connect a receptacle (Customer Supplied) or cable to the input power lines and the system ground per the U.S. National Electrical Code and any applicable local codes. For cords over 100 foot, larger copper wires should be used. Fuse the two hot lines with super lag type fuses as shown in the following diagram. The center contact in the receptacle is for the grounding connection. A green wire in the input cable connects this contact to the frame of the welder. This ensures proper grounding of the welder frame when the welder plug is inserted into a grounded receptacle. CONNECT TO A SYSTEM GROUNDING WIRE. SEE THE UNITED STATES NATIONAL ELECTRICAL CODE AND/OR LOCAL CODES FOR OTHER DETAILS AND MEANS FOR PROPER GROUNDING. CONNECT TO HOT WIRES OF A THREE-WIRE, SINGLE PHASE SYSTEM. *.1035"/5/05&4 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JTIPVMECFDPOOFDUFEUPBEFEJDBUFECSFBLFS  FTQFDJBMMZXIFODPOOFDUFEUP7"$ 5IF1PXFS.*(.1JJTOPUSFDPNNFOEFEGPSVTFXJUIFYUFOTJPOT DPSET*GBOFYUFOTJPODPSENVTUCFVTFE FOTVSFJUJTDPOTUSVDUFEXJUI BNJOJNVNPGHBHFXJSFT LOCATION AND MOUNTING The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. will operate in harsh environments. Even so, it is important that preventative measures are followed in orderto assure long life, reliability, and safe operation. • The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. must be located in an area with circulation of clean air such that air movement in the back and out the front louvers. • Dirt and dust that can be drawn into the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. should be kept to a minimum. Failure to observe these precautions can result in excessive operating temperatures and nuisance thermal trips. HIGH FREQUENCY PROTECTION During operation, distance the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. from radio controlled machinery. The normal operation of the Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. may adversely affect the operation of RF controlled equipment, which may result in bodily injury or damage to the equipment. evidence.text: GUN AND CABLE INSTALLATION

The Magnum® PRO 175L gun and cable provided with the Power MIG® 215MPJ5. is factory installed with a liner for .025-.035" (0.9-1.2 mm) wire and an .035" (0.9mm) contact tip. The user shouldensure that the contact tip, liner, and drive rolls match the size ofthe wire being used.

evidence.text: GENERAL MAINTENANCE In extremely dusty locations, dirt may clog the air passages causing the welder to run hot. Blow dirt out of the welder with low-pressure air at regular intervals to eliminate excessive dirt and dust build-up on internal parts.

nodes.name: Wire drive mechanism requires routine maintenance

properties.name: Wire drive mechanism requires routine maintenance
properties.description: Wire drive mechanism requires routine maintenance

evidence.text: After every coil of wire, inspect the wire drive mechanism. Clean it as necessary by blowing with low pressure compressed air. Do not use solvents for cleaning the idle roll because it may wash the lubricant out of the bearing. All drive rolls are stamped with the wire sizes they will feed. If a wire size other than that stamped on the roll is used, the drive roll must be changed.

nodes.name: Wire feed unit turns off

properties.name: Wire feed unit turns off
properties.description: Wire feed unit turns off

evidence.text: WIRE FEED OVERLOAD PROTECTION

The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. features overload protection of the wire drive motor. If the motor becomes overloaded, the protection circuitry turns off the wire feed unit. Check for the proper size tip, liner, and drive rolls, for any obstructions or bends in the gun cable, and any other factors that would impede the wire feeding. To resume welding, simply pull the trigger. There is no circuit breaker to reset.

nodes.name: Wire feeding problems
aliases: Wire-feeding problems

properties.name: Wire feeding problems
properties.description: Wire feeding problems

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: WIRE FEED OVERLOAD PROTECTION

The Power MIG® 215 MPJ5. features overload protection of the wire drive motor. If the motor becomes overloaded, the protection circuitry turns off the wire feed unit. Check for the proper size tip, liner, and drive rolls, for any obstructions or bends in the gun cable, and any other factors that would impede the wire feeding. To resume welding, simply pull the trigger. There is no circuit breaker to reset.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

conditions.text: If the procedures are not understood or the maintenance or repairs cannot be performed safely
Before service, maintenance, or repair, fully disconnect power to the machine.
Use PPE, including safety glasses, a dust mask, and gloves; this also applies to persons entering the work area.
A liner cut for one gun should not be installed in another gun unless it meets the liner cutoff-length requirement.
Have qualified personnel perform all maintenance and troubleshooting work.
Moving parts can injure: do not operate with doors open or guards off; stop the engine before servicing; keep away from moving parts.

notes: one end is not named in the source

evidence.text: Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.

To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

NOTE: The variation in cable lengths prevents interchanging of liners between guns. Once a liner has been cut for a particular gun, it should not be installed in another gun unless it can meet the liner cutoff length requirement.
Before carrying out service, maintenance and/or repair jobs, fully disconnect power to the machine.

MOVING PARTS can injure. • Do not operate with doors open or guards off. • Stop engine before servicing. • Keep away from moving parts.

evidence.text: Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.

To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.
Before carrying out service, maintenance and/or repair jobs, fully disconnect power to the machine.
Use Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, dust mask and gloves to avoid injury. This also applies to persons who enter the work area.
MOVING PARTS can injure. • Do not operate with doors open or guards off. • Stop engine before servicing. • Keep away from moving parts.

conditions.text: If feed problems are experienced after the liner has been cleaned and blown out until no further dirt comes out

notes: one end is not named in the source
reviewer: The manual says to replace the liner if feed problems persist after cleaning and blowing it out until no further dirt comes out; it does not say the liner remains dirty.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.

conditions.text: If cleaning has been done and feeding problems are experienced
Before service, maintenance, or repair, fully disconnect power to the machine.
Have qualified personnel do all maintenance and troubleshooting work.
Do not operate with doors open or guards off; stop engine before servicing; keep away from moving parts.
If you do not understand the procedures or cannot safely perform maintenance or repairs, contact a Lincoln Authorized Service Facility for technical troubleshooting assistance before proceeding.
Use PPE, including safety glasses, dust mask, and gloves; this also applies to persons entering the work area.

evidence.text: To help prevent feeding problems, clean cable liner after using approximately 300 pounds (136 kg) of electrode. Remove the cable from the wire feeder and lay it out straight on the floor. Remove the contact tip from the gun. Using an air hose and only partial pressure, gently blow out the cable liner from the gas diffuser end.
Flex the cable over its entire length and again blow out the cable. Repeat this procedure until no further dirt comes out. If this has been done and feed problems are experienced, replace the liner.
